Hi Sophia — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the RFP. Looping in Markus (pricing) and Sean (SE) — I'll pull a short mapping doc and a CSV for procurement.

High level (quick notes while we prep the attachments):
- Chat Completions (new API model): billed per-token for prompt + completion. Same token math as Responses when both are used with a token stream, but the SDK-level semantics differ (Chat has structured messages).
- Responses (unified responses API): usually billed per "response unit" which we translate back to tokens for cost comparisons. For most text generation workloads you can expect Responses and Chat to be comparable on a per-token basis, but we provide explicit mappings below in the CSV.
- Legacy endpoints: we still accept legacy calls; billing is normalized to Responses for hosted accounts but we show a breakdown line-item so procurement can see the original endpoint SKU mapped to the unified unit.

I'll attach the CSV (billing-mapping.csv) and our latest ratecard (ratecard_v2.pdf). Markus — can you confirm typical discount guidance for a 6-month commit?

Hi Sophia — Sean here from Solutions Eng. I attached the CSV and a short worked example below; Camila has already shared the ratecard.

Short worked examples (illustrative):
- Example A: Chat Completions (structured messages)
  - Prompt tokens: 300
  - Completion tokens: 150
  - Billed tokens = 450 tokens per call.
  - If ratecard lists $0.004 per 1K tokens, cost = 0.45 * $0.004 = $0.0018 per call.

- Example B: Responses (unified API)
  - Responses returns an aggregated "response unit" that we map to tokens for invoicing: the same exchange above maps to ~450 tokens for invoicing. For typical text utils, margin differences are negligible.

- Legacy endpoint calls
  - We normalize legacy endpoint metrics to the Responses unit for hosted billing. Procurement will see two columns in the CSV: original legacy SKU + normalized token invoice value. The legacy SKU is retained for historical visibility.

When to prefer Responses vs Chat from a cost standpoint:
- If you use many short prompt/short responses, per-call overhead can make Chat slightly more economical if you leverage streaming/realtime.
- If you need one-shot multi-modal outputs or prefer a simpler SDK, Responses can be easier to integrate; cost aligns once normalized to tokens.

Discount guidance (subject to legal signoff):
- 3-month commit (hosted): 5–10% depending on volume
- 6-month commit: 10–18% (higher end if you commit to >= 5M tokens/mo)
- Annual commit: 18–30% sliding by volume and prepay.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Sophia: share expected tokens/month and % streaming vs batch.
2) We’ll run an invoice example and produce a short procurement-ready one-pager (CSV + sample invoice).
3) If the volume aligns, Camila + Markus will propose a term sheet.

Attached: billing-mapping.csv (CSV, 1 KB) — includes per-endpoint mappings and sample calc.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if that helps.
